page: Microsoft Azure E96pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epdsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated physical cores powered by Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processors operating at 3.4 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 672.0 GB of RAM, providing 7.0 GB of memory per core, and a substantial 5669 GB of local storage. This instance is also Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier performance characteristics, particularly in multi-core and memory-bound workloads. The server achieves top-tier rankings in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core score, and Passmark memory score. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, scoring in the top tier for both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached read and write operations. Database and web serving capabilities are also highly rated, with top-tier performance in Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and Passmark database operations. Single-core performance, however, remains in the average tier across stress-ng and Geekbench tests.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E96pds_v6 offers high resource density by combining a massive 96-core ARM architecture with 672.0 GB of memory and over 5.6 TB of local storage. This makes it an efficient choice for scale-out workloads that benefit from physical core dedication and high memory bandwidth without the overhead of hyperthreading. Appropriate workloads include large-scale databases, Redis caching layers, high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded software compilation, and medium-to-large LLM text generation tasks where its memory capacity and multi-threaded decompression capabilities can be fully utilized.
